text:
Dr. Ben Hinds
Psychiatry Registrar
Maroubra Hospital
Lakes Road
Maroubra

7/3/2011
Dear Dr. hinds,
RE: Yuxiang Meng
Thank you for seeing Mr. Meng, a 21-year-old Chinese student chef whose features are suggestive of acute manic disorder. He lives with his uncle at the same home and he knows the basic English. 
On 2/3/2011, Mr. Meng presented with upper respiratory tract infection. However, he was observed to have elevated mood. He had delusions and was talking about fixing the world's nuclear waste problem. On examination, manic episode was suspected. Accordingly, he was referred to the local community mental health team. Diazepam 10 mg was also prescribed. 
On the next day, the mental health team provisionally diagnosed that it was non dangerous mania. However, they were keen to avoid hospitalization   because the patient was afraid of psychiatry ward. Therefore, the patient was commenced on quetiapine. They recommended also decreasing the frequency of Diazepam to be twice per day.
On today review, the patient's uncle reported that Mr. Meng had discarded his medications. He also reported that last night he was running naked down the street. On examination, he was very elevated in mood with exaggerated previous delusions. He stripped nude and tried to hug me.  Diazepam 20 mg and quetiapine were prescribed but he refused to take any medications.
In view of the above, I am referring this patient for your further assessment and management. For any queries, please contact me.
Yours sincerely
Doctor
